nodes.label: Super-admin AI briefing and Q&A over cross-tenant product feedback
Hard caps on corpus size are the only defence against a context-length error or a surprise OpenAI bill
Feedback text is fenced as untrusted DATA between markers so a feedback item cannot issue instructions
Super-admin gate must live at the application layer because every query runs on a service-role client that bypasses RLS
Tenant display name is company_name — the tenants table has no bare name column
Fenced-JSON theme extraction degrades to an empty theme list rather than failing the summary
Browser-supplied chat history is truncated so a stuck loop cannot push a megabyte per keystroke
Backfill a missing stripe_payment_intent_id on a payment row via three escalating Stripe lookups
Lookups must run on the Stripe platform the payment was CREATED on (payments.platform_account, default 'uk' legacy)
Fallback matching by amount within a +/-1 day window, then by customer email — heuristic, can bind the wrong PaymentIntent
Every failure path returns HTTP 200 with success:false — the portal reads the body, not the status
Every Stripe call is retried without the stripeAccount option, because older records were written on the platform account
Mirror Veriff document-front/back and face images into Supabase Storage and stamp the verification row
Veriff requires an HMAC-SHA256 signature over the media id (not the whole request) alongside the API key
Identity documents are written to the public customer-documents bucket and a public URL is persisted on the verification row
Per-image failures return null and are skipped; the run still reports ok with whatever it managed to store
Finalize a Pay-As-You-Go rental: post a final pro-rated partial day, then close the rental
R5: a paused PAYG rental is not billed for the dormant time — the admin paused deliberately
service_role bypasses RLS, so tenant ownership of the rental is re-verified inside the function
Partial-day accrual is claimed through the unique day-index constraint, with a 23505 retry when the accrual cron wins the race
A failed ledger insert deletes the claimed accrual row so the day index is not burned
Pro-rated partial day: daily rate by hour, tax by percentage, fixed service fee scaled by hours covered
Vehicle is flipped back to Available on close — safe because the DB overlap trigger allows only one non-terminal rental per vehicle
Cached AI expense narrative per (tenant, scope) for the portal expenses tabs
Deliberately free of ../_shared imports so it deploys cleanly via the Supabase Management API
Highlight chips are computed in code so the displayed numbers can never be hallucinated by the model
Re-implements the OpenAI usage ledger inline over raw PostgREST, including its own hardcoded price constants
expense_ai_summaries.summary holds a JSON string (headline/narrative/insights/highlights), not prose
Tenant reporting export (CSV/XLSX) across payments, P&L, rentals, statements, fines and aging
A client-supplied tenantId is never trusted: super admins may target any tenant, everyone else is pinned to their app_users row
Six reporting views back the exports: view_payments_export, view_pl_by_vehicle, view_rentals_export, view_customer_statements, view_fines_export, view_aging_receivables
Column headers carry the tenant's currency symbol, resolved from tenants.currency_code
PDF export is an explicit 501 stub — only CSV and XLSX exist
Files are returned as a JSON envelope (content/filename/mimeType), base64 for XLSX — the browser does the download
Cron that generates monthly verification and expiry reminders for customer insurance policies
reminder_events.unique_key encodes policy + milestone; a 23505 duplicate is swallowed so repeat cron runs emit nothing
Expiry ladder fires at exactly 30, 14, 7 and 0 days before expiry
Policies past expiry are flipped Active to Expired; the source query only pulls Active, so the lapse alert fires exactly once
The always-on operator bell is tied to the newly-created reminder_event — this is the portal bell the reminder_events ledger never fed
One gated operator digest email per tenant per run instead of per-policy mail, each send isolated so email cannot break reminder generation
AI summary of internal staff reviews of a customer, cached in customer_review_summaries
The subscription hard block was enforced in the BROWSER only, so a grace-expired tenant could keep driving billable endpoints with a saved JWT
Prompt forbids addressing the customer — the summary is staff-facing only
When every review is skipped or deleted the cached summary row is deleted rather than left stale
Public per-tenant Apply form shape: hidden steps, required-field overrides and welcome message
lead_management_enabled=false makes the whole Apply endpoint 403 — the feature toggle is enforced server-side
Tenant resolved from the x-tenant-slug header with a body tenantSlug fallback, because the endpoint is unauthenticated
Fetch a rental's signed agreement — stored copy first, live BoldSign download as fallback
rentals.docusign_envelope_id still stores BoldSign document ids — the column name outlived the DocuSign integration
BoldSign mode is resolved from rentals.boldsign_mode, falling back to the tenant, so an old test document is fetched with the test key
PDF is base64-encoded in 0x8000 chunks to avoid a String.fromCharCode stack overflow on large documents
A stored signed_document_id short-circuits the BoldSign call — important in test mode where documents auto-delete after 14 days
Resolve whether the booking flow takes payment automatically or is manual/enquiry-based
Portal stores 'automated'/'manual' but the booking flow expects 'auto'/'manual' — this function is the translation seam
Precedence chain: tenant_settings.payment_mode, then global org_settings.payment_mode, then org_settings.booking_payment_mode
Any error returns mode 'manual' with HTTP 200 — failing towards not charging a card is the safe direction
Mint a Stripe Connect account_onboarding link for a tenant, returning to the portal Stripe Connect settings tab
Connect onboarding always uses the LIVE secret key and refuses with 503 unless it starts with sk_live_ — a test key would onboard nobody
tenantId is taken from the request body with no membership check — unlike the billing functions that call authorizeTenantAccess
Consolidated statement of account across every rental a customer holds in one tenant
RLS is off on ledger_entries and view_customer_statements is a security-definer view granted to anon — this function IS the tenant boundary
Two caller modes: a customer_users row yields only its own statement (client customerId ignored); an app_user may name any customer of its own tenant
Paid is derived as charged minus remaining; raw Payment rows are ignored because they can predate FIFO application
Fixed display order for charge categories, with account-level (rental_id NULL) charges grouped last
DB/schema error text never reaches the client of a financial endpoint — errors are logged and a generic message returned
Serve the client the right Stripe publishable key and mode for a tenant, resolved by slug or id
Only tenants with status='active' resolve — a suspended tenant cannot obtain a publishable key
Return the tenant's platform subscription row plus live Stripe data with payment method and latest invoice expanded
The Stripe account recorded on the subscription row wins over the tenant's current config; rows predating the UAE migration default to 'uk'
A Stripe retrieval failure is logged and swallowed so the DB subscription still renders — billing UI must not go blank on a Stripe outage
Drive 917 admin booking notification email for chauffeur and close-protection bookings
Brand name, phone number and address are hardcoded into the template — this function predates the tenant-branded email path
Close-protection bookings are detected by string-sniffing the vehicle name for a shield emoji or the phrase itself
No auth, no tenant lookup and no database access — it emails whatever address the caller supplies via Resend
Cache-through INSHUR/ABI Period Z eligibility check for one or many vehicles
Fails CLOSED, the deliberate inverse of bonzah-check-vehicle-eligibility: a false positive puts an uninsured rental on the road
A verdict that could not be obtained is never written to the cache — a thirty-second ABI outage must not leave a whole fleet marked red
Three consecutive transport failures open a circuit breaker; remaining vehicles are reported unchecked rather than hammering a dead ABI
A 60s network deadline reserves isolate time to write results and respond instead of being killed mid-batch
A cached verdict is only reusable when mode, VIN and TTL all still match — a simulated pass must never stand in for a real one
Malformed vehicle ids are filtered before the query because Postgres would fail the whole batch on one bad uuid
Vehicles are read scoped to the tenant: membership proves who the caller is, not that the vehicle ids they sent are theirs
Start INSHUR/ABI Period Z cover for one rental: eligibility, renter, rental period, ID card, coverage row
ABI has no idempotency key, so the pending row is claimed through idx_inshur_cov_one_active BEFORE the billable call
A 23505 on the claim is the guard working: the concurrent winner's coverage is returned instead of buying a second policy
An ambiguous create (timeout/network/5xx) leaves the row pending so the unique index keeps holding the rental against a second policy
Failures are persisted as coverage rows with status failed/ineligible and a real error code — never swallowed, never merely logged
A rental's existing terminal-failure row is reused so attempt_count reads as attempts for that rental and the list shows one line per uninsured rental
Cover starts at the first instant of the pickup day and ends at the last minute of the return day — four other files default these times differently
date and time columns are concatenated verbatim; routing them through a Date would reinterpret them in the isolate's UTC zone
Garaging state: vehicles.garaging_state is authoritative, then free-text state extraction from pickup, delivery and tenant addresses
ABI has no renter-update endpoint, so a SHA-256 hash of the sent fields forces re-registration when a customer corrects their details
ID-card extension and content type are derived from ABI's FILETYPE because the payload format is undocumented and may change
The private bucket's storage PATH is stored, not a URL, and simulated cards carry the mode in both the path and the filename
Cover is already active when the ID card is fetched, so an ID-card failure is a warning on a successful response, never a rollback
PostgREST 42703 on the vehicles.garaging_state embed is reported as INSHUR_SCHEMA_INCOMPLETE rather than sending an operator hunting their own data
Cancelled, Rejected and Closed rentals are refused outright — buying cover for them is real money spent on nothing
Pay-as-you-go and open-ended rentals cannot be insured: every ABI rental period needs an exact start and end
Usage type defaults from the rental/customer gig-driver flag but is operator-overridable, because it decides whose name is on the ID card
Uninsured-rental alerting: an unlatched reminders upsert keyed on ux_reminders_identity plus a once-daily deduped operator bell
Alert severity is critical once the rental has already started and warning before it — the same rule in create, end and cancel
End INSHUR/ABI Period Z cover on a rental that has already started
End and Cancel are deliberately NOT gated on getInshurUsability: cover already bought must always be stoppable even after INSHUR is switched off
ABI answers a failed End with a bare {}, so a Get Rentals probe on the VIN decides whether the period is genuinely gone before anything is written
Ending a real policy while the tenant sits in simulated mode would mark it ended locally while it keeps billing at ABI — refused with 409
On failure the coverage status is left untouched: recording it as ended would hide cover that is still being billed
Cover ended at ABI but the row update failed — reported as INSHUR_RECORD_WRITE_FAILED so nobody retries the ABI call
A simulated policy has no ABI counterpart, so it is closed locally even after the tenant moves to real credentials
Cancel INSHUR/ABI Period Z cover that has not started yet, falling back to End once it has
ABI permits Cancel only before the period begins; after that the call is switched to End and the response says so plainly, because they are not the same thing to an operator
start_time_sent is compared against 'now' rendered into the same zone and format, making it a plain string comparison with no offset arithmetic to get wrong
inshur_rental_coverage.rental_id is ON DELETE SET NULL, so a coverage can outlive its rental — and that orphan is exactly the row still billing
A claimed row with no inshur_rental_id and no error code never reached ABI, so it is simply closed locally
Both camelCase and snake_case body keys are accepted, and coverage_id targets one specific row for a rental that has been re-covered
Repeated pattern: a service-role client bypasses RLS, so tenant scope is re-derived from app_users inside the function and never taken from the client

Pay-As-You-Go close-out: pro-rated partial day, accrual claim against the cron, ledger rows, rental close and vehicle release
Service-role tenant re-scoping repeated across five unrelated edge functions because RLS is bypassed
